flags.quote: Moving your f3-knight to e5 gives the opponent more access to your king. A better move would have been moving your pawn to c3.
flags.critique: This is a 505-centipawn piece blunder and you lectured me about king safety. The knight left f3, which was holding d4; Black plays Bxe2, forcing Qxe2, then Qxd4+ forks the king and the knight you just parked on e5. c3 would have shored up d4, but the lesson is 'you hung a pawn and then a piece,' not 'the opponent got more access to your king.'

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e2 with your g4-bishop is the strongest move because you fork the white queen and the white f1-rook and you take the defender of the white queen.
flags.critique: I am not forking queen and rook. White just recaptures. Be2 was not 'the defender of the white queen' — it was attacking it. The whole point is a decoy: take the bishop so the queen leaves d1, then Qxd4+ wins the hanging knight. You sold me a fake fork and hid the combination.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on f1 with your f8-rook is the strongest move because you fork the white b1-knight and the white king and then pin the knight to the rook.
flags.critique: My queen is hanging to Be3. I am not forking Nb1. This is a zwischenzug: take on f1 with check before you deal with the attacked queen, pull the king to f1, then grab the knight. 'Pin the knight to the rook' is leftover geometry that never happens. Teach the in-between move.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your f-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: The pawn is defended by the g7-bishop. I can see the diagonal. Calling it undefended is a lie; if anything White is betting Black should not recapture because d4 takes the bishop. Say it is a pawn trade, or that recapturing with the bishop hangs it, but do not tell me a piece I can see defending 'was undefended.'

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f4 leaves you with a backward pawn. A better move would have been taking the pawn on d6 with your e-pawn.
flags.critique: exd6 is the right better move. The diagnosis is not. After d4-e5-f4 that e-pawn is a spearhead with two supports, not a backward pawn. The real knock is you refused the exchange on d6, pushed another pawn, and invited dxe5 with the queen staring down the d-file. Wrong structure word, right alternative.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to e3 is the strongest move because you skewer the black queen, exposing the black pawn.
flags.critique: I am in check from Qd4. Be3 blocks the check and hits the queen. That is the lesson. A 'skewer' of the queen that 'exposes a pawn' (a7 sitting behind it) is decorative nonsense. Stop promoting pawn-backs into tactics textbooks.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the move the whole Modern is waiting for: hit the e5 spearhead. You gave me a bare 'strongest move' with empty reasons. If you cannot say 'challenge the advanced pawn' on the one move that does it, what is the coach for?

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your queen on the white pawn and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: The queen discovering onto d4 is real. 'Take the defender of the white pawn' is not: e5 does not defend d4, pawns do not protect sideways. You also tagged doubled pawns that do not exist. Teach: you chop the spearhead and the queen eyes d4. Leave the defender-of-the-pawn riddle out.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e5 with your queen is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Yes, take the hanging knight. Then the sentence falls apart: 'and then pin the pawn to the rook' has no subject and names no pawn. That pin is leftover detector junk from Qxd4 still echoing. One true clause, then a grammar crash.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on f1 with your king is the strongest move because the rook was undefended.
flags.critique: The rook was checking me. I recapture with the king because that is how you get out. It was not undefended; I was the defender. You also stuffed king_safer and pawn_shield onto a king that just got dragged to f1. Recapture is not 'winning material.'

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e2 with your queen is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Forced recapture after Bxe2. Calling it winning an undefended bishop is the same lie as Kxf1. Net zero, queen pulled off d1, and now Qxd4+ lands. If you must talk, say you had to recapture and the queen left the d-file.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f6 is playable, but moving your pawn to c5 would be better.
flags.critique: Better how? c5 is the Modern/Pirc hit on d4. f6 also hits e5 but rips my king and invites exf6. Empty reasons on an inaccuracy is just 'the engine liked the other pawn.' Tell me which break and why f6 is the ugly one.

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to e4 is playable, but moving your b8-knight to c6 would be better.
flags.critique: 86 centipawns, two identical discovered_attack tags, and still no because. Nc6 develops and piles on d4; Ne4 looks cute and then White can just ignore it or I walk into Ne5 chaos. 'There's better' without a reason is a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your king to g1 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: I am in check from Rf8. Kg1 steps out of check. There is no f-pawn to save. You invented a hanging pawn so you would have a because-clause. 'Get out of check' is enough.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c3 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: Recapture again, and your own reasons already knew doubled_pawns and isolated_pawn. Then the sentence you spoke was 'undefended.' I now have doubled isolated c-pawns; that is the cost of taking back. Surface the structure you already detected.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is playable, but moving your b1-knight to c3 would be better because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: e5 is the overextension, not a center-scoring contest. The pawn becomes a target for d6/c5 and you have not developed. Nc3 is better because it develops and keeps the duo; 'claim more of the center' is the same phrase you used for e4 and d4.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to e2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You just praised Bg4 for pinning the knight to the queen. Be2 is how you break that pin. Development got dropped as tautology and I am left with a naked 'strongest move.' Teach unpinning on the unpin.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: It is the Modern. The pawn is going to g6 so the bishop can live on g7. Empty reasons, 37 centipawns of 'best,' and 'That's the one.' I learned nothing I could reuse on move two of this opening.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to g7 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: Call it a fianchetto. The bishop belongs on the long diagonal; that is why we played g6. 'Pressure on the center' is the same slot you use for every pawn push. I already know the bishop looks at d4 — say that.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your queen is the strongest move because you fork the white e5-knight and the white king and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: The fork of king and Ne5 is the actual tactic and you almost taught it. Then you bolted on 'pin the pawn to the rook,' which pawn, which rook, and it is not why I took on d4. One true idea plus a hallucinated pin.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to c4 is the strongest move because you fork the black king and the black e4-knight.
flags.critique: Geometry of a fork, sure. They play Kh8 and the knight does not fall; it is protected. You lost 75 centipawns and still called it strongest because of a fork that wins nothing. Call it a check that improves the queen, not a winning fork.

flags.quote: Moving your rook to f8 is the strongest move because your rook gets an open file and it forces the king to respond.
flags.critique: Bc3 just skewered my queen. I do not meekly move the queen; I check on f8 first. Second zwischenzug of the game and you said 'open file.' The check is real. The lesson is: answer the skewer with a check.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c3 with your bishop is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: I am taking the bishop my queen and g7-bishop both hit. That is it. Pin-the-pawn and defender-of-the-pawn are detector leftovers from earlier captures. Stop stacking fake tactics onto a recapture of the piece you just discovered onto.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f6 with your e-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You tagged hanging, but f6 is defended by e7 and the bishop. The real story is I offered a kingside rip and you took it. Empty 'strongest' plus a false hanging tag. Say you smash the structure / take the offered pawn.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f6 with your g8-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: It is a recapture that develops the knight. 'Undefended' and 'wins material' treat a pawn I just lost as a free gift. Tell me I recapture toward the center and get a piece out. Same template as fxe5, Qxe2, Kxf1, Bxd2, bxc3.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures winning and undefended
suggestions.detail: wins_material copy says 'the X was undefended' whenever SEE ≈ piece value. That fires on equal recaptures (fxe5, Nxf6, Qxe2, Kxf1, Bxd2, bxc3) and on defended pawns where recapturing is unprofitable. Gate wins_material on net material vs the previous ply, or require the captured unit to have zero defenders before saying undefended. A 1200 can see the bishop on g7; the lie is instant distrust.

suggestions.title: Drop forks, skewers, and pins that win nothing
suggestions.detail: selectBecauseReasons always prefers two tactical kinds, so geometric forks (Bxe2 vs Q+R, Rxf1 vs K+Nb1, Qc4+ vs K+N) and pawn-back skewers (Be3 vs Q and a7) crowd out the real idea. Keep a tactic only if a target is hanging, the back piece is not a mere pawn, or eval actually moves. Also stop concatenating a second pin with followUp ('and then pin the pawn to the rook') when the pin is relative junk on a recapture square.

suggestions.title: Detect in-between checks while a piece hangs
suggestions.detail: Rxf1+ and Rf8+ are the same pattern: opponent just attacked a queen, you check (or capture-check) first. Add a zwischenzug / in_between kind when the mover gives check and an own unit was hanging or just became the front of a skewer. Phrase-bank: 'you take with check before dealing with the threat.' This is the lesson a club player actually needs from this game.

suggestions.title: Pick the blunder concept from the refutation line
suggestions.detail: Ne5 lost a piece via Bxe2 Qxe2 Qxd4+, but chooseConcept preferred king_safety because king_more_exposed/back_rank fired. If summarizeLine shows a net piece or pawn, rank hanging/removed_defender/refutation_material above king_safety. Suggested c3 is fine as a stabilizer, but the spoken problem must be the hung d4 pawn and the knight that dies with check, not 'access to your king.'

suggestions.title: Name the next forcing move on a combo starter
suggestions.detail: Bxe2 is only 'best' because Qxd4+ comes next. Line events already exist in select-insight; when the played capture is not itself the material win, surface the follow-up ('so the queen leaves d1 and Qxd4+ forks king and knight') instead of the landing-square fork of Q and R. Same slot would have saved Rf8+ vs the Bc3 skewer.

suggestions.title: Never ship a better-move with empty reasons
suggestions.detail: f6 vs c5, Ne4 vs Nc6, and e5 vs Nc3 all said 'X would be better' with nothing after. If contrastBenefits is empty, fall back to a concrete slot: suggested pawn-break (c5 hits d4), developing the last knight, or not pushing the spearhead. A 1200 will ignore every inaccuracy that does not say why.

suggestions.title: Add fianchetto, undermine, and unpin reasons
suggestions.detail: g6, Bg7, d6, Be2, and e5 all fell through to center_control or silence. In opening phase, detect fianchetto (bishop to g2/g7/b2/b7 after the wing pawn), undermining an advanced enemy pawn (d6 vs e5), and breaking a pin (Be2 vs Bg4). Phrase-bank lines beat 'pressure on the center' for the first eight plies of a named opening.

suggestions.title: Do not let SEE crowd out doubled and isolated pawns
suggestions.detail: bxc3 already had doubled_pawns and isolated_pawn in the reason list; selectBecauseReasons threw them away because wins_material is tactical. For recaptures, prefer structure kinds when capturedSeeCp is not a real gain. Same bug hid the useless doubled_pawns tag on dxe5 — filter structure that did not actually appear, but when it did, say it.

whatWorked: Bg4: 'you pin the knight to the queen' is the actual idea, in one clause.
Nxd2+: fork of queen and king plus the discovered hit on the e3-bishop is the real tactic.
Bc3: skewer of queen exposing the g7-bishop is a genuine skewer, unlike Be3 vs a pawn.
Qe3+: fork of bishop and king, and the bishop unveils onto c3 — both true.
Qd3: 'saves your queen from capture' after Qf4 eyed it — simple and correct.
Castling: mentioning the open f-file is actually useful in this pawn-stripped structure.
On f4, suggesting exd6 was the right better move even though 'backward pawn' was the wrong why.
